result.topic_en: Scholium 3 (§22) of Euler's paper on vibrating elastic laminae, working out the case ω ≈ 3.9: it computes the ordinates at the two ends E, F and the midpoint O, shows the midpoint ordinate is negative as in the figure, and begins computing the tangent slopes at these points.
result.transcription:
$\gg$ ) 125 ( $\ll$
Scholion 3.
§. 22. Quo haec clarius perſpiciantur, caſum primum, quo $\omega = 3,9$ circiter, ideoque eius ſinus negatiuus, accuratius perpendamus. Erit igitur, primo factore, conſtante ſeu a tempore pendente, omiſſo:
$y = - - - - e^{u\omega} + e^{\omega(1-u)} + (1-e^{\omega})\,\mathrm{ſin.}\,u\omega + (1+e^{\omega})\,\mathrm{coſ.}\,u\omega,$
cuius valores pro tribus caſibus $u=0$, $u=1$ et $u=\frac{1}{2}$ definiamus, vt applicatas non ſolum pro vtroque termino E et F, ſed etiam pro puncto medio O, ſcilicet E$e$, F$f$ et O$o$ obtineamus. Primo igitur, poſito $u=0$ erit E$e = 2(1+e^{\omega})$; poſito autem $u=1$, prodit applicata
$\mathrm{F}f = e^{\omega} + 1 + (1-e^{\omega})\,\mathrm{ſin.}\,\omega + (1+e^{\omega})\,\mathrm{coſ.}\,\omega,$
qui valor, ob $\mathrm{ſin.}\,\omega = -1$ et $\mathrm{coſ.}\,\omega = \frac{2}{e^{\omega}+e^{-\omega}}$, abit in hunc:
$\mathrm{F}f = 2(1+e^{\omega})$, ſicque hae duae applicatae E$e$ et F$f$ inter ſe erunt aequales; at pro puncto medio O, vbi fit $u=\frac{1}{2}$, hincque $\mathrm{ſin.}\,\frac{1}{2}\omega = \mathrm{ſin.}\,\frac{3}{2}\varrho = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ et $\mathrm{coſ.}\,\frac{1}{2}\omega = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, erit applicata
$\mathrm{O}o = e^{\frac{\omega}{2}} + e^{\frac{\omega}{2}} + \frac{(1-e^{\omega})}{\sqrt{2}} - \frac{(1+e^{\omega})}{\sqrt{2}} = 2e^{\frac{\omega}{2}} - e^{\omega}\sqrt{2},$
qui valor, ob $e^{\omega} = 111$ et $e^{\frac{\omega}{2}} = 10\frac{1}{2}$, abit in $21 - 111.\sqrt{2}$; vnde patet, hanc applicatam eſſe negatiuam, prorſus vti figura refert. Poſſumus etiam ſimili modo poſitionem tangentium pro his locis exhibere ex formula
$\left(\frac{dy}{ds}\right) = - - - e^{u\omega} - e^{\omega(1-u)} + (1-e^{\omega})\,\mathrm{coſ.}\,u\omega - (1+e^{\omega})\,\mathrm{ſin.}\,u\omega;$
quae formula, poſito $u=0$, pro termino E praebet:
$\left(\frac{dy}{ds}\right) = 1 - e^{\omega} + 1 - e^{\omega} = 2(1-e^{\omega}) = -2(e^{\omega}-1);$
Q 3 tum

items.quote: caſum primum, quo $\omega = 3,9$ circiter, ideoque eius ſinus negatiuus, accuratius perpendamus
items.english: Let us examine more accurately the first case, where ω ≈ 3.9 and hence its sine is negative.

items.quote: ſicque hae duae applicatae E$e$ et F$f$ inter ſe erunt aequales
items.english: And thus these two ordinates Ee and Ff will be equal to each other.

items.quote: vnde patet, hanc applicatam eſſe negatiuam, prorſus vti figura refert
items.english: Whence it is clear that this ordinate is negative, exactly as the figure shows.

items.quote: Poſſumus etiam ſimili modo poſitionem tangentium pro his locis exhibere
items.english: We can also in a similar way exhibit the position of the tangents at these places.
